title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let X be a simplicial set (an object of Δ^ = Ss) and k a commutative ring, in practice a field. Let Ab_{k*} be the category of simplicial k-modules. Grothendieck attaches to X the k-linear functor

F_X : Ab_{k*} → Ab_k, M ↦ Hom_{Δ^}(X, M) ≅ Hom_{Ab_{k*}}(k[X], M).

So F_X is co-represented by the linearization k[X], with k[X]_n = k^{(X_n)}. He also considers the generalization G_λ = Hom(λ, -) for an arbitrary simplicial module λ (here λ = C_*(X) = k[X]).

The 'test objects'. From the previous page, C^i_* = Λ^{i+1} L_* is the simplicial k-module whose normalized (Dold–Kan) complex is k in degrees i and i+1 (a 'disk'). Here L_n = k^{Δ^n}. The C^i assemble into a cosimplicial–simplicial object C^·_*. Its value at [n] is the normalized cochain complex of Δ^n, namely Λ^{·+1} k^{n+1} = k^{Inj(Δ^·, Δ^n)}.

The idea is that a k-additive functor F on simplicial modules is to be probed by the complex F(C^·_*) = (i ↦ F(C^i_*)). For F = F_X one gets

F_X(C^i) = Hom(X, Λ^{i+1}L) = C^i(X),

the normalized (non-degenerate) i-cochains, which form a subspace of k^{X_i}. Thus F_X(C^·) is the normalized cochain complex C^·(X) = C_·(X)^∨. More generally G_λ(C^i) ≅ λ_i^∨. Example: F_{Δ^n}(M) = M_n.

The construction. For X finite, he looks at the simplicial k-module

[n] ↦ Hom(F_X, F_{Δ^n}) ≅ Hom_·(C^·(X), C^·(Δ^n)) ≅ Hom_·(C^·_{[n]}, λ^{·∨∨}) ≅ (λ^{∨∨})_n = k[X_n]^{∨∨}.

This gives a commutative square:
- left column: X_n ≅ Hom(Δ^n, X) → k[X_n] → k[X_n]^{∨∨}, the last map an isomorphism if X_n is finite;
- right column: Hom(Δ^n, X) → Hom(F_X, F_{Δ^n}) ≅ Hom(C^·(X), C^·(Δ^n)).

Specializing X = Δ^m gives k[Δ^m_n] = k[Hom(Δ^n, Δ^m)] ≅ Hom(F_{Δ^m}, F_{Δ^n}). In other words, the full subcategory spanned by the cochain functors of simplices is the k-linearized category Δ (opposite).

Purpose. This is the linear prototype of reconstructing a simplicial set from its cochains by the 'spatial realization / Spec' functor A ↦ ([n] ↦ Hom(A, C^·(Δ^n))). Linearly one only recovers k[X], the linear Yoneda statement. The next page ('pas linéaire!', with Hom of Λ^{·+1}k^{Δ} and Γ, i.e. divided powers) shows him moving to a nonlinear, multiplicative or divided-power structure on cochains to recover X itself. This sits inside his 1975–76 programme on the divided-power de Rham complex as a model of homotopy types.
errors: The line C^·(Δ^n) ≅ Λ^{*+1}k^{Δ^n} = (m ↦ k^{Hom_ens(Δ^m,Δ^n)}) is inaccurate. Normalized m-cochains of Δ^n are functions on the injective monotone maps Δ^m → Δ^n (dimension binom(n+1, m+1)), as the previous page correctly states (k^{Inj_Δ}). They are not functions on all set maps.

By the k-linear Yoneda lemma, Hom(F_X, F_{Δ^n}) ≅ Hom(k[Δ^n], k[X]) = k[X_n] holds exactly, with no finiteness needed. The double dual and the hypothesis 'X_n finite' only enter through the second identification with Hom of cochain complexes. That identification replaces F_X by its values on the cochain objects C^i, and is valid only under finiteness. The diagram is correct, but the arrow labelled iso into k[X_n]^{∨∨} conflates the two steps.

The claim that a k-additive functor F is determined by the complex F(C^·_*) is only asserted. It needs F to commute with the relevant (co)limits, or finiteness hypotheses; this is a gap, not an error, for representable F_X with X finite.

ideas.what: Represent a simplicial set by the k-linear functor Hom(X, -) on simplicial modules and probe it on the Dold–Kan 'disk' objects C^i, recovering the normalized cochain complex C^·(X) = F_X(C^·).
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan correspondence / normalized cochains as a corepresented functor
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses linearization and Dold–Kan-type material extensively (1983); not this exact formulation

ideas.what: Simplicial module [n] ↦ Hom(C^·(X), C^·(Δ^n)) and the comparison map X → k[X] → k[X]^{∨∨} ≅ this object (linear 'spatial realization' of the cochains, the unit of a cochains/Spec adjunction).
ideas.modern_name: Linear version of Sullivan spatial realization ⟨A⟩ = Hom(A, Ω(Δ^•)); Toën's affine stacks Spec(C^*(X)); Mandell's cochain models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977), Bousfield–Gugenheim (1976); Toën (2006, building on Grothendieck's schematization idea); Mandell (2001, 2006)
ideas.where_published: Schematic homotopy types are sketched in Pursuing Stacks (1983); this cochain-Spec construction is not there in this form as far as I know

ideas.what: The full subcategory of cochain functors F_{Δ^m} is the linearized simplex category: k[Hom(Δ^n, Δ^m)] ≅ Hom(F_{Δ^m}, F_{Δ^n}).

missed.claim: In 1975–76, in the context of the divided-power de Rham complex, Grothendieck sets up the 'Spec of cochains' functor [n] ↦ Hom(C^·(X), C^·(Δ^n)) and the comparison X → Spec C^·(X). He then notices (next page, 'pas linéaire!') that one must use nonlinear, divided-power structure on cochains to recover X rather than k[X]. This anticipates the idea, later realized by Mandell (E∞ / p-adic) and Toën (affine stacks, cosimplicial algebras), that homotopy types in positive or mixed characteristic are recovered from cochains with extra multiplicative or divided-power structure. Here it is tied explicitly to divided powers, about 7 years before Pursuing Stacks.
missed.quote: On s'intéressera, pour X_* fini, à [n] ↦ Hom(F_{X_*}, F_{Δ^n_*}) ≃ Hom_·(C^·(X_*), C^·(Δ^n_*))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This dates Grothendieck's thinking on cochain-algebra models of homotopy types, and on 'schematization', to 1975–76, linked to divided-power de Rham. That is relevant to the history of affine stacks and integral/p-adic homotopy theory. The page itself only does the linear, routine case.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is routine (Yoneda plus Dold–Kan, giving back the linearization). Its interest is historical: it shows Grothendieck in 1975–76 setting up the cochain 'spatial realization' functor and heading toward nonlinear, divided-power structures to recover the space. This foreshadows affine stacks and Mandell-type theorems, but contains no new finished result.
transcription_corrections: '(m ↦ k^{Hom_ens(Δ^m,Δ^n)})' in the image looks like k^{Hom_Δ...} / k^{Hom_ens...}; mathematically it should be injective maps (Inj_Δ).
'Plus gén., G_{λ_*}(C^i_*) ≃ λ^∨_i' is circled in the margin, as a side remark.
'(cochaînes non dég.)' — the scribble is 'non dég.' (normalized cochains), confirming the corrected reading.
The bottom line reads 'Faisons en particulier X_* = Δ^m_*, on trouve donc'.
